title: Gyroid bones + gyroid sheet, double-wall variant
description: Two complementary gyroid bone solids (offset -1.2, Lipschitz 1.5) combined with a thin gyroid sheet (shell 0.2) and clipped to a sphere.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: offset applied to the gyroid field (bones)

parameters.name: lipschitz
parameters.description: field rescale for safe sphere tracing

constraints.why: sphere tracing under-estimates distance when the field slope exceeds 1; lipschitz>=1 is the correctness gate
shell 0 collapses the sheet to the iso-surface

nomination.reason: gyroid sheet vs bones are two different lattice topologies; Atta v1.2 only plans lattice.gyroid_slab

title: Schwarz P minimal surface (bones + thin sheet + morph)
description: Schwarz P as a closed-form field -(cos x+cos y+cos z); bones via offset(-1), a shell(.2) sheet, and a morph blend between a cube and its intersection with the sheet.

title: Neovius surface as a two-line distance field
description: dist = -(3*(cos x + cos y + cos z) + 4*cos x*cos y*cos z), shelled and clipped to a cube. The cheapest possible TPMS primitive: one expression.

parameters.name: lipschitz
parameters.description: large rescale needed: the Neovius gradient is much steeper than gyroid

constraints.why: Neovius needs ~10x rescale; smaller values alias badly
a sheet thicker than half the cell period merges both labyrinth halves into a solid block

title: 2D circular lattice: shelled circles on a repeat_xy grid
description: shell 0.2 of a circle radius 2, repeated on a 2x2 pitch, unioned with a translated copy to close the interstice.
code:
let
    c = repeat_xy [2,2] << shell .2 << colour black << circle 2;
in
union[c,translate[1,1]<<c]

constraints.why: pitch below the diameter makes rings overlap instead of tiling
a ring wall thicker than its own radius closes the ring into a disc

title: Menger sponge by recursive difference with repeated cutout
description: Recursive level n: build a cutout of extruded squares (2/3^(i+1)) on a 2/3^i repeat grid, subtract it and its two axis reflections from a cube.

constraints.why: 3^6=729 cells/axis; above that the mesh count explodes

nomination.reason: recursive subspace subtraction is the cheapest route to high-genus solids; Atta has no recursion in Spec v3

topology_note: recursive fractal genus metadata was a level-1 value; not reliable

title: Engrave an implicit gyroid pattern into a solid (depth-limited)
description: engrave depth pattern target = target minus (shell(depth) of target intersected with pattern).  Depth-limited surface texturing, the implicit analogue of text_engrave.

parameters.name: emboss_t
parameters.description: morph parameter for the emboss twin

constraints.why: engraving deeper than half the body removes the body
pattern coarser than the part reads as a hole, not a texture

nomination.reason: generalises text_engrave to any implicit pattern at fixed depth — exactly what a 'surface finish' op needs

title: Gyroid3D(scale Vec3) — the canonical triply-periodic field
description: Gyroid with independent per-axis period (scale v3.Vec). The period is the only knob; wall thickness comes from offsetting the field, as in Curv.

constraints.why: extreme per-axis periods break the isotropy that makes a gyroid printable in any orientation
a non-positive period makes the field constant or mirrored

title: minkowski() — the sum that turns a tool shape into an offset operator
description: minkowski() is the Minkowski sum of its children: sweeping one child's shape over the other. The manual's own example rounds a 10x10x1 box with a cylinder(r=2,h=1) and states the resulting outer size is 14x14x2 — the extents add. Critically, the origin of the second object is used for the addition, so centring the tool changes which directions grow.

parameters.name: tool_radius
parameters.description: radius of the rolling tool (cylinder r in the manual's example)

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: $fn of the tool; cost is the product of both children's fragment counts

constraints.why: manual states the outer dimensions become 10+2+2 by 10+2+2 by 2 — the tool's extent adds on both sides
manual: 'the origin of the second object is used for the addition', so a non-centred tool grows the base asymmetrically
manual warning: combining two children with $fn=100 performs 100*100 = 10000 operations, and memory grows with it

nomination.reason: one op that covers rounded edges, knurling, thickening a lattice strut and inflated shells — Atta lists minkowski as unmapped

notes: Paraphrase of the minkowski section, including its two warnings (cost product, and that a compound second child is treated as separate inputs unless unioned first).

title: libfive gyroid(period, thickness): period and wall thickness as the only knobs
description: The libfive stdlib exposes the triply periodic minimal surfaces as two-parameter fields: `gyroid(period, thickness)` (and the Schwarz P sibling). period sets the cell size, thickness sets the wall — the same pair Atta's planned lattice.gyroid_slab needs, expressed as a field rather than a mesh.

constraints.why: a wall thicker than half the cell merges the two labyrinth halves and the lattice becomes solid
sub-0.4mm walls are below FDM nozzle resolution

notes: Signature read from the generated libfive python stdlib (MPL-2.0 kernel layer; the GPL-2+ part of libfive covers the Studio binary only — see NOTE.md licence table).

title: libfive array_x / array_xy / array_xyz / array_polar_z: repetition in field space
description: libfive's stdlib makes repetition a field operation with an explicit count and delta per axis, plus a polar form. Because the array is a field, the copies blend and clip exactly like the source shape — no per-copy mesh bookkeeping.

constraints.why: pitch below the shape extent fuses neighbours into one solid — sometimes wanted (a lattice), usually a surprise
field evaluation cost is linear in copy count, and meshing is worse

notes: Signatures read from libfive's generated python stdlib (array_x, array_xy, array_xyz, array_polar_z).

title: Menger-style sponge by 8-neighbour recursion (offset table)
description: fractal() scales the hole to w/3, appends it at a position, then recurses into the 8 surrounding offsets unless depth == maxDepth. The 8-offset table *is* the sponge rule; the same rule appears in Curv's menger example, which is a good cross-language confirmation of the family.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: current cell width; divided by 3 each level

code:
from manifold3d import Manifold
import numpy as np


def fractal(holes, hole, w, position, depth, maxDepth):
    w /= 3
    holes.append(hole.scale([w, w, 1.0]).translate([position[0], position[1], 0.0]))
    if depth == maxDepth:
        return
    offsets = np.array(
        [
            [-w, -w],
            [-w, 0.0],
            [-w, w],
            [0.0, w],
            [w, w],
            [w, 0.0],
            [w, -w],
            [0.0, -w],
        ]
    )
    for offset in offsets:
        fractal(holes, hole, w, position + offset, depth + 1, maxDepth)


def posColors(pos, _):
    return [-p + 0.5 for p in pos] + [1.0]


def run(n=1):
    result = Manifold.cube([1, 1, 1], True)
    holes = []
    fractal(holes, result, 1.0, np.array([0.0, 0.0]), 1, n)

    hole = Manifold.compose(holes)

    result -= hole
    result -= hole.rotate([90, 0, 0])
    result -= hole.rotate([0, 90, 0])

    return (
        result.trim_by_plane([1, 1, 1], 0)
        .set_properties(4, posColors)
        .scale([100, 100, 100])
    )

constraints.why: 8^maxDepth holes: depth 4 is 4096, depth 6 is 262144 and the boolean cost explodes
the hole must be rescaled by w/3 at every level or the recursion stops being self-similar

topology_note: recursive fractal genus metadata was a level-1 value; not reliable
